userStories.title: RORCA_AGENT Environment Variable and Config Schema
userStories.description: Introduce RORCA_AGENT env var (values: 'claude' | 'opencode' | 'codex') and RORCA_MODEL (e.g. 'openai/gpt-4o', 'google/gemini-2.0-flash', 'anthropic/claude-opus-4-6') to backend config. Claude subscription remains default. OpenCode path activates when RORCA_AGENT=opencode. Codex CLI path (ChatGPT subscription) activates when RORCA_AGENT=codex.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/.env supports RORCA_AGENT=claude|opencode|codex (default: claude)
backend/.env supports RORCA_MODEL=<provider>/<model> (used when RORCA_AGENT=opencode)
backend/src/lib/config.ts exports agentType and agentModel with validation on startup
Invalid RORCA_AGENT value throws descriptive error on startup
GET /api/config returns { agentType, agentModel } for frontend display
CLAUDE.md documents both env vars with examples

userStories.title: OpenCode Binary Detection and Version Check
userStories.description: On backend startup, detect whether the opencode binary is installed and accessible when RORCA_AGENT=opencode. Surface clear errors if missing.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend startup checks for opencode binary via 'which opencode' or equivalent when RORCA_AGENT=opencode
If opencode not found: log clear error 'OpenCode not installed. Run: npm i -g opencode' and exit with code 1
GET /api/health returns { opencodeVersion, opencodeInstalled } when agentType=opencode
Version check runs 'opencode --version' and parses semver output
Minimum supported version constraint documented in CLAUDE.md

userStories.title: OpenCode Server Lifecycle Manager
userStories.description: When RORCA_AGENT=opencode, manage an OpenCode server process that stays warm across stories using the --attach flag. Start the server before the first story, reuse it for all subsequent stories in a run, shut it down after run completes.
acceptanceCriteria: New backend/src/lib/opencode-server.ts manages server lifecycle
start(): spawns 'opencode server' with detached:true, captures server socket/port
attach(): returns --attach flag value for use in story execution
stop(): gracefully terminates server process after run completes or on error
Server PID stored alongside pipeline_runs.pid in DB
If server crashes mid-run, backend attempts one restart before marking run failed
Server startup timeout: 10s before giving up
Logs server stdout/stderr to os.tmpdir()/rorca-opencode-server.log

userStories.title: execution-engine.ts Agent Switching Logic
userStories.description: Update backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts to detect RORCA_AGENT and switch the per-story subprocess accordingly. When opencode, spawn 'opencode run --format json --attach' instead of 'claude --print'. This is the single TypeScript execution engine — run-loop.sh and run-loop.ts are fully replaced by this file.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts reads agentType from config (default: claude)
When agentType=claude: existing 'claude --print' spawn path unchanged
When agentType=opencode: spawns 'opencode run --model $RORCA_MODEL --format json --attach $ATTACH_ADDR' with prompt via stdin
When agentType=codex: spawns 'codex --approval-mode auto-edit' with prompt via stdin
ATTACH_ADDR passed from opencode-server.ts lifecycle manager via function argument, not env var
Story timeout implemented via AbortController (no gtimeout/bash timeout — TypeScript only)
Exit code captured from child process 'close' event
All three paths produce WAL events (story_started, story_passed, story_failed) via the same emitter

userStories.title: OpenCode JSON Event Stream Parser
userStories.description: Parse opencode's --format json event stream output into the same format Rorca's SSE pipeline expects. Map JSON events to terminal output and semantic log entries.
acceptanceCriteria: New backend/src/lib/opencode-parser.ts parses JSON event stream from opencode run --format json
Extracts tool calls (bash, edit, read, write, glob, grep) into semantic log entries
Converts raw JSON events back to human-readable terminal output for xterm.js display
Detects story completion signal from event stream
Handles partial/chunked JSON lines (streaming parser, not bulk parse)
Error events mapped to story failure detection
Unit tests cover all event types in backend/src/lib/__tests__/opencode-parser.test.ts

userStories.title: Pipeline Trigger — OpenCode Run Spawn
userStories.description: Update POST /api/pipeline/trigger to use the OpenCode server lifecycle and pass correct env vars when RORCA_AGENT=opencode.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/pipeline/trigger detects agentType from config
When opencode: starts OpenCode server via opencode-server.ts before calling execution-engine.ts
Passes agentType, agentModel, and opencode attachAddr directly to execution-engine.ts as function arguments (not env vars)
Strips Claude-specific env vars (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, etc.) when using opencode
Server lifecycle tied to pipeline run: server stops when run finishes/fails
pipeline_runs table stores agent_type and agent_model columns (migration required)
GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id returns agentType and agentModel fields

userStories.title: Database — Agent Type Columns on pipeline_runs
userStories.description: Add agent_type and agent_model columns to pipeline_runs. Per CLAUDE.md architecture, column additions use the pragma table_info check pattern in backend/src/db/index.ts — NOT a numbered migration SQL file (migrations 001–036 already exist; using a numbered file risks collision).

agent_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claude' added to pipeline_runs if column not present
agent_model TEXT (nullable) added to pipeline_runs if column not present

userStories.title: Error Handling and Fallback for OpenCode Path
userStories.description: Robust error handling when OpenCode binary fails, crashes mid-story, or returns unexpected output. Graceful degradation without leaving orphan processes.
acceptanceCriteria: If opencode run exits non-zero: story marked failed with OpenCode error message in WAL
If OpenCode server crashes mid-run: attempt one restart, then mark entire run failed with clear message
If JSON event stream is malformed: log raw output and attempt story-level recovery
Orphan process cleanup: on backend restart, kill any opencode server PIDs from crashed runs
Cleanup runs on startup: scan pipeline_runs WHERE status='running' AND agent_type='opencode', kill PIDs, mark failed
User-facing error message distinguishes: 'OpenCode not installed', 'Provider API key invalid', 'Model not available', 'Rate limit exceeded'
Rate limit detection: parse 429 from JSON event stream, surface as 'Rate limited — waiting Ns' in terminal

userStories.title: Story Complexity Scorer — Model Tier Assignment
userStories.description: Analyze each story before spawning its subprocess and assign a ModelTier (haiku | sonnet | opus) based on story complexity signals. Eliminates blind Opus usage for every story — routes cheap work to cheap models.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/complexity-scorer.ts exports score(story) → { tier: 'haiku'|'sonnet'|'opus', score: number, signals: string[] }

Scoring signals: dependsOn depth (+10 per level), acceptanceCriteria count (+5 each), file path patterns (docs/**→-20, src/core/**→+20), story type tag (docs→haiku, test→sonnet, feat→sonnet/opus, architecture→opus)
Keyword detection in description: 'rename'/'update import'/'fix typo' → haiku; 'refactor'/'migrate' → sonnet; 'design'/'architect'/'implement from scratch' → opus
Score thresholds configurable in .rorca/config.json orchestration.thresholds (default: 0-30→haiku, 31-65→sonnet, 66+→opus)
ModelTier maps to actual model IDs per provider in orchestration.cascades config
Scorer runs synchronously before subprocess spawn — adds <10ms overhead
Score + signals logged to WAL event payload for FinOps tracking
Unit tests cover all scoring signals and threshold boundaries

userStories.title: Cascading Escalation Engine
userStories.description: When a story fails on a cheaper model tier, automatically escalate to the next tier and retry. Haiku fails twice → Sonnet. Sonnet fails → Opus. Ensures quality without over-provisioning expensive models upfront.
acceptanceCriteria: Escalation config in .rorca/config.json: orchestration.escalation.maxRetriesOnTier (default: 2), orchestration.escalation.escalateTo mapping
execution-engine.ts tracks retry count per story per tier via run-state.json
On story failure: check retry count vs maxRetriesOnTier — if exceeded, escalate model tier and retry
Escalation chain: haiku → sonnet → opus (stop at opus, no further escalation)
WAL event written on escalation: { type: 'story_escalated', fromTier, toTier, attemptNumber, storyId }
Run View shows escalation indicator in story list: 'Escalated: Haiku→Sonnet (attempt 3)'
Escalation disabled for claude --print subscription path (model fixed at story level, not mid-story)
Escalation adds actual cost for escalated attempts to FinOps tracking
Config option: orchestration.escalation.enabled (default: true) — can disable for predictable billing

userStories.title: Orchestration Config in .rorca/config.json
userStories.description: Expose the full model routing and cascading configuration in .rorca/config.json so advanced users can customize routing thresholds, model assignments per task type, and escalation behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: .rorca/config.json gains top-level 'orchestration' section
orchestration.router: 'auto' (complexity scorer) | 'fixed' (use spec model for all stories) | 'manual' (per-story overrides in spec JSON)
orchestration.cascades: { echolocation, planning, coding, lintFix, testing, documentation } → model IDs per task type
orchestration.escalation: { enabled, maxRetriesOnTier, chain: ['haiku','sonnet','opus'] }
orchestration.thresholds: { haiku: [0,30], sonnet: [31,65], opus: [66,100] }
orchestration.tokenBudgetPerStory: max input tokens before warning (default: 50000)
Settings > Execution Engine > Model Routing section exposes these fields visually
Visual: three-tier slider showing haiku/sonnet/opus threshold boundaries with drag handles
JSON schema updated in .rorca/config.schema.json
backend/src/lib/config.ts validates orchestration section on load with descriptive errors

userStories.title: Codex CLI Execution Path — ChatGPT Subscription Support
userStories.description: Add 'codex' as a third RORCA_AGENT value, enabling users with a ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription to use OpenAI's Codex CLI as the per-story execution engine. Like claude --print, this is subscription-based (flat-rate, no per-token cost), so model cascading and FinOps dollar savings do not apply. Codex CLI runs non-interactively via --approval-mode auto-edit, giving it the same tool set (file edit, bash, read, write, glob, grep) as Claude Code.
acceptanceCriteria: RORCA_AGENT=codex activates Codex CLI path in backend/src/lib/config.ts
Binary detection: check PATH for 'codex' binary, surface clear error if not found with install instructions (npm i -g @openai/codex)

backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts spawns 'codex --approval-mode auto-edit' as a child process per story, with the story prompt passed via stdin — same TypeScript spawn pattern used for the opencode path (OC-003)
Codex CLI stdout/stderr is captured and streamed to xterm.js the same way claude --print output is — no structured JSON parsing required
RORCA_MODEL is ignored when RORCA_AGENT=codex (Codex CLI uses the model tied to the user's ChatGPT subscription)
Settings UI shows 'Codex CLI (ChatGPT subscription)' as a third agent option alongside Claude and OpenCode
Settings UI shows install check: green tick if 'codex' is in PATH, red warning with install command if not
FinOps dashboard shows token count only for codex path (no dollar cost — subscription users pay flat rate, same treatment as claude --print)
Model cascading is disabled when RORCA_AGENT=codex — no tier assignment, no escalation
CLAUDE.md and Settings docs updated with codex setup instructions
